stem: (Select TWO.) Birchwood Freight's configuration accidentally gives two entirely different providers the same preferred local name. Which TWO statements correctly describe how to resolve this?

choices.text: Give each provider a distinct `source` address in its own declared entry, but keep both entries under the same local name.
Delete the block that declares each provider's version constraint entirely, so Terraform infers both providers automatically from the resource types used.
Give both providers the same `alias`; `alias` is what distinguishes one provider package from another.
Combine each provider's namespace with its type name into a compound local name joined with a dash, so both providers can be referenced without colliding.
Each argument inside the `required_providers` block enables exactly one provider, so the two colliding providers still need two separate entries there regardless of naming.

rationale: A compound local name that joins each provider's namespace and type with a dash lets both be referenced without colliding, and each still needs its own entry in `required_providers` because each argument there enables exactly one provider. Terraform requires a unique local name for each provider in a module, so pointing two entries at distinct `source` addresses while keeping them under the same local name does not resolve the collision; the local name itself is still shared. Deleting `required_providers` removes the version-constraint declaration and does not resolve a naming collision. `alias` distinguishes multiple configurations of the same provider, not two different providers, so giving both the same alias does not address this at all.
